text:
will: Heads-up — ran into a weird case in the Go generator streaming sample app where cancelling the parent context didn't stop the server-side work. Repro steps below.

emily: ugh ok, can you paste the minimal snippet?

will: yeah — simplified: ```ctx := context.Background() // mistake
stream, err := client.Generator().Stream(ctx, req)
for { tok, err := stream.Recv() ... }```

sam: immediate smell: using Background for a request you expect to cancel. But is the stream actually honoring ctx cancel?

will: that's the thing — client side sees ctx cancelled, Recv() returns context.Canceled, but on the server/runtime we still had an active KV cache and a job slot tied up for ~15s. If you retry immediately it fails quoting "handshake already in progress" in logs.

jen: do we think this is auth/retry related or generator handshake lifecycle? Could be the client closed the read but didn't send explicit EOF during the streaming handshake so the server waited for completion.

will: logs show a 101 (stream started) then no final chunk; server timed out after the runtime's default idle window. But we also observed a token refresh happening at the same time in other runs, so maybe the auth retry path is racing with the cancel path.

emily: interesting. I remember a similar note in the Python lib where they send a cancel frame during websocket shutdown. Our Go gRPC-ish implementation just closes the transport which sometimes doesn't reach the runtime quickly.

sam: propose we (1) add docs for sample app to always pass ctx from the request handler, (2) add a small integration test that simulates context cancel during handshake and asserts resources freed, (3) consider exposing a Stream.Cancel() method that sends a short control frame before closing.

will: +1 on tests/docs. For API ergonomics: today we have client.Generator().Stream(ctx, req) and users forget ctx. Maybe we should provide a convenience helper NewCancelableStream(ctx, client, req) that returns a wrapper with Cancel() so it's obvious.

jen: downside: more surface area to maintain. Alternatively we could change the generator Stream to return a stream object that embeds a context-aware cancel func in the returned value: stream, err := client.Generator().Stream(ctx, req) // stream.Cancel() available even if ctx was Background

emily: I like the latter — minimal API churn, still ergonomic. Also let's ensure auth refresh doesn't re-do handshake without aborting outstanding stream; add a short-circuit that if ctx.Done() fired we cancel retry attempts.

will: filed a tiny GH issue with repro + logs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/issues/312 (draft). Sample app will be updated in onboarding repo.

sam: for the sample app text, add a short explanation: "Prefer passing the incoming request context to any generator/stream call to ensure cancellations from client requests propagate to inference runtime".

jen: ci-bot ran a quick lint on the sample and flagged a missing defer stream.Close(). We should add a pattern example showing defer stream.Close() and explicit stream.Cancel() in handlers.

emily: I'll sketch the README patch and a tiny test harness for the handshake-cancel case. We'll also add a comment in the auth retry code: if ctx.Done() then return early.

will: thanks — blocked on a runtime owner to approve the server-side change to honor cancel frames. @sam do you want to loop in runtime eng?

sam: looping @runtime-team in #eng-runtime, pinging internal runtime leads. I'll paste the logs and link to the GH issue.

ci-bot: Added label "dx-onboarding" to issue #312 and triggered integration job `stream-handshake-cancel-test`.

will: cool — assigning to emily for the SDK patch and to runtime for server behavior. I'll update the onboarding sample once PRs land. :thumbsup:
